So E126's late-update effect is not explained by standard theory, and smaller late batches (bs 768 in the final 32 px slice) are not ruled out by it. (7) Sampled or approximate weight gradients, a new FLOP lever: published results are weak (3.5% speedup on ResNet-20, about 0.9 pp loss on WRN CIFAR-100 at 50% channels). Low prior.

I searched for outside evidence on the open hypotheses and for directions the tree has not tried. Main results:

(1) H9.2.2, lookahead removal. airbench94_muon, the Muon CIFAR-10 reference whose lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6 the tip inherited, uses no lookahead or EMA at all; hiverge's record does not list any either. Under Muon, airbench's lookahead is not part of the reference design, so the 100-seed removal test is worth running. A null result would bank about 0.4% time. This conflicts with E092 (-0.18 pp, 8 seeds), which only the 100-seed test can settle.

(2) H2.18.3, stochastic depth. MosaicML's guidance says to avoid stochastic depth, or use a small drop rate, in nets with few blocks. The +2.8 pp / -25% time result is for ResNet-110 trained for hundreds of epochs. This lowers the prior further.

(3) New lever: Muon-C (arXiv 2609.09676, Sep 2026). It takes a 3x3 DFT of each conv kernel's momentum and orthogonalizes each of the 9 complex Cout x Cin frequency blocks, instead of the unfolded [Cout, 9*Cin] matrix. Reported gains are largest early and on short budgets: same quality at 0.62x model FLOPs, and +0.4-0.6 pp top-1 on ImageNet-100 ResNet-34/50. Steps are 16% slower than unfolded Muon there (99.4 vs 86.0 ms/step, 1.36x vs Adam). My own estimate of its cost here, not from the paper: about 3.7x the NS FLOPs (1 real block plus 4 complex conjugate pairs, done as 2Cout x 2Cin real matrices), i.e. +4-5 ms/step if FLOP-bound. That is roughly +20-25% time. It only pays if it buys about 1 pp, or if it is used only in the cheap 16/24 px phases, where the paper says the gain concentrates. Its 5 fp32 NS steps would also need porting to bf16 with 3 steps. This is the only outside lead I found for buying accuracy.

(4) Dynamic data pruning (InfoBatch, PFB). Results are lossless only on long schedules (about 200 epochs). Under an aligned pruning ratio, InfoBatch loses accuracy noticeably on CIFAR-100. Given E012 and E124 (unique coverage matters at 32 px), the prior is low.

(5) Late batch size. Gradient-noise-scale theory (1812.06162) says the critical batch grows late in training. That conflicts with E126 (bs 1536 late cost 0.18 pp). So E126's late-update effect is not explained by standard theory, and smaller late batches (bs 768 in the final 32 px slice) are not ruled out by it. E126's rate (~0.07 pp per 1%) beats the 0.05 slope.

(6) FreezeOut computes BN statistics in inference mode for frozen layers. That supports arm (b) of H2.20.5 (BN eval in the frozen window) as faithful to the source, though its saving is small.

(7) Sampled or approximate weight gradients, a new FLOP lever: published results are weak (3.5% speedup on ResNet-20, about 0.9 pp loss on WRN CIFAR-100 at 50% channels). Low prior.

(8) Other CIFAR-100 speedrun repos (RyanChong0117, Daniel-T-S-Adams) only list the organizer's 59.3 s ResNet9 baseline; I found no competing public recipe faster than the tree's. The futurebiohackers repo URLs used as tree sources now return 404.

findings.claim: airbench94_muon (the Muon CIFAR-10 record recipe: Muon lr 0.24, momentum 0.6 Nesterov, bs 2000, 8 epochs, LS 0.2, translate 2, filter renorm p *= sqrt(len(p))/||p|| in the Muon step) contains no lookahead and no weight EMA. Biases are trained by SGD at lr 0.053 and the head at lr 0.67. The whitening bias trains for 3 epochs.
findings.relevance: Under Muon, the tip's lookahead-EMA is an SGD-era inheritance that the reference Muon recipe dropped. This is outside support for running the 100-seed lookahead-removal test (H9.2.2), which banks ~0.4% time if null. It conflicts with E092's -0.18 pp (8 seeds, ~1.4 SE).

findings.claim: The hiverge 1.98 s CIFAR-10 record lists these changes: vectorised Muon (padded batched NS, periodic renorm), vectorised crop, brightness/contrast augmentation, a compiled fwd+bwd step, GELU->SiLU, SVD whitening, fp16 + channels_last, selective TTA and retuned hyperparameters. It mentions no lookahead/EMA and no layer freezing.
findings.relevance: A second Muon SOTA recipe with no reported training-time averaging, supporting H9.2.2's test. Its augmentation and activation changes were already tested and failed here on CIFAR-100 (E003, E008), and TTA is banned.

findings.claim: 'If using a model with only a few blocks, it is best to use a small drop rate or to avoid stochastic depth.' Huang et al.'s 25% time cut with +2.8% CIFAR-100 accuracy used ResNet-110 at drop_rate 0.5. ResNet-50 on ImageNet at drop 0.2 gave only ~5% wall-clock saving at equal accuracy. The optimal drop rate scales with depth.
findings.relevance: The tip has 3 groups with 2 residual convs each, the regime where MosaicML advises against stochastic depth. This lowers H2.18.3's prior further. With 2/3/3 costing -0.29 pp (E127), a per-batch random skip of the same branch is unlikely to lose >=0.05 pp less at equal expected saving.

findings.claim: Muon-C (Operator-Aligned Muon for Convolutional Kernels, Sep 2026) applies an orthonormal 2D DFT over the 3x3 kernel grid. It orthogonalizes each of the 9 complex Cout x Cin frequency blocks with NS (5 fp32 complex iterations in the paper), inverse-DFTs back (the result stays real via conjugate symmetry) and rescales to RMS 0.2. ImageNet-100 top-1, 100 epochs: ResNet-34 80.22 vs unfolded Muon 79.64; ResNet-50 79.88 vs 79.28; ConvNeXtV2-T 84.88 vs 84.62. The advantage is 'most pronounced early': CIFAR-10 flow matching FID 9.87 vs 22.26 at 40k steps, 3.47 vs 3.83 at 400k, and the same quality at 0.62x model FLOPs. Step time is 99.39 ms vs 86.02 ms for unfolded Muon.
findings.relevance: This is the only outside lead I found for buying accuracy (+0.4-0.6 pp over unfolded Muon, with the gains largest on short budgets). The tree needs a funded accuracy source after the margin ran out (H4.9). Cost is the risk. My estimate, not from the paper: 1 real plus 4 complex conjugate-pair blocks, done as 2Cout x 2Cin real matrices, is ~3.7x the NS FLOPs of the [Cout, 9Cin] form, i.e. +4-5 ms/step (~+20-25% time) if FLOP-bound. It is viable only if ported to bf16 with 3 iterations and/or confined to the early 16/24 px phases. Proposed new H7 child: Muon-C on group filters in the low-res phases only, 100-seed test, needs >= +0.15 pp at <= +2% time.

findings.claim: Partial Forward Blocking reports CIFAR-100 full-data accuracy 78.2% vs InfoBatch 78.1% (actual pruning ratio only ~25%) and PFB 78.8% at 50% pruning. It states: 'Aligning the actual pruning ratio reveals a significant performance drop for InfoBatch on CIFAR-100', which it attributes partly to the large gradient weights on retained samples. Other dynamic methods at 50% lose up to 3.4 pp (UCB 75.3, eps-greedy 74.8). These are long-schedule ResNet runs.
findings.relevance: Dynamic data pruning, a direction the tree has not considered (InfoBatch claims 33-40% lossless savings on CIFAR-100), is fragile on CIFAR-100 even on long schedules. With E012 (selective backprop -0.64 pp) and E124 (halving unique coverage at 32 px cost -0.82 pp), the prior is low. If it is tried at all, only in the 16/24 px phases using the previous epoch's stored losses (no extra forward).

findings.claim: McCandlish et al.: the gradient noise scale predicts the largest useful batch size (including on CIFAR-10), and it increases as the loss falls during training, so the critical batch size grows in late training.
findings.relevance: Standard theory predicts that late phases tolerate larger batches. E126 found the opposite (bs 1536 at 28/32 px cost -0.18 pp, while extra early updates were worth +0.00, E121). The late-update effect is therefore unexplained, possibly a Muon or test-resolution effect, and theory does not close the bs-768-at-the-very-end direction retired in H2.11.5. E126's rate (~0.07 pp per 1%) beats the 0.05 slope (E128), so a bs-768 final slice (e.g. the last 0.5-1 epoch at 32 px) could be a funded accuracy source worth one 100-seed test.

findings.claim: FreezeOut: frozen layers are 'put in inference mode and excluded from all future backward passes', and 'a frozen layer's batchnorm costs are reduced (no longer having to calculate means and variances)'. The forward is still computed and activations are not cached. Recommended defaults: cubic schedule with LR scaling, t0=0.8. WRN on CIFAR-100: ~20% speedup without accuracy loss in the best configs; DenseNets lose ~3%.
findings.relevance: Supports arm (b) of H2.20.5 (BN eval mode in the frozen window) as faithful to the source; arm (a), the LR anneal, was already null (E129). Activation caching is irrelevant here because the frozen window covers <1 pass per image. Gains in FreezeOut come from long schedules and progressive per-layer freezing.

findings.claim: Approximating filter weight gradients in backward (keeping only the largest-magnitude gradient per output channel) on every 4th conv layer gave a 3.5% wall-clock speedup with 0.1% accuracy loss on ResNet-20 CIFAR-10. Related: channel-sampled tensor ops on WRN-28-10 CIFAR-100 at 50% channels gave 77.1% vs 78.0% (1805.08079).
findings.relevance: A new FLOP/energy lever, approximate wgrad, could transfer to the energy-bound judge. The evidence is weak, though: small speedups and ~0.9 pp CIFAR-100 loss at 50% sampling, far worse than the 0.05 pp per 1% yardstick. Low prior; not recommended over depth or width arms.

findings.claim: airbench96_faster: 45 epochs, bs 1024, SGD lr 9, momentum 0.85, wd 0.012, bias_scaler 64, LS 0.2, whiten_bias_epochs 3, flip + translate 4 + cutout 12, widths 128/384/512 at depth 3. Lookahead uses alpha = 0.95**5 * (step/total)**3 every 5 steps. Selective backprop keeps the top 512/1024 by proxy-model loss (proxy widths 32/64/64, depth 2). The airbench paper: airbench94 64/256/256 with 2 convs/block, 9.9 ep, translate 2; airbench95 128/384/384 with 2 convs/block, 15 ep; airbench96 128/512/512 with 3 convs/block, 40 ep, cutout 12.
findings.relevance: Translate 4 and cutout appear only in the 40-45-epoch recipes; every short (<=15 ep) recipe uses translate 2. That keeps H12.3.1's prior low at ~7.5 epochs. airbench also moves to 3 convs/block only at the longest budget, which is weak outside support for depth cuts (H2.18) on short schedules. E127 still measured -0.29 pp for 2/3/3, and 3/3/2 (-6.1% projected) has no accuracy measurement yet.
